why: Three independent grounds, each shown with arithmetic. (1) Notice mechanics: OA §6.3 requires written notice delivered to each Member by CERTIFIED MAIL AND EMAIL at least 30 days before the due date; the 2026-08-20 call was a texted PDF — no certified mail was ever attempted (undisputed in the Manager's own production), and the only email address on file has been dead since 2019. Under Zimmerman v. Crothall, as summarized in the library, dilution provisions are enforced as written but the issuer must comply strictly with the specified delivery mechanics; a call that fails the specified delivery method does not trigger dilution. CERTAINTY-WEIGHTING (updated after client answers): the client did receive actual notice (she saw the texted PDF) and defendants will argue no prejudice — she could not have funded $270,000 regardless — so the delivery defect may be treated as excusable in practice; this ground is pleaded but the arithmetic ground is the lead theory. No valid call -> no Dilution Event -> §9.2's book-value buyout trigger never fired. (2) The dilution arithmetic does not reconcile even internally: at the Manager's own asserted $7.2M fair value, standard pro-rata dilution of a member who funded none of a $1.5M raise yields 0.18 x 7.2/8.7 = 14.90% (new money priced at pre-money value) or 0.18 x (7.2-1.5)/7.2 = 14.25% (if $7.2M is post-money) — not 6.1%. Back-solving the notice's 6.1% for Bram (82% -> 93.9%) requires valuing the post-money company at P where 0.18 x (P-1.5M)/P = 6.1%, i.e. P = 1.5M/(1-0.061/0.18) = $2,268,877 post-money (implied pre-money $768,877). The notice's own arithmetic therefore values the company at 3.2x LESS than the $7.2M the Manager himself asserted. (3) The Manager's $7.2M 'fair value' is 27% below the contemporaneous independent broker opinion ($14.5M enterprise value; $9.8M equity). Valuation gap at a glance: offer $189,100 (6.1% x $3.1M book) is 31.6% of $597,800 (6.1% x $9.8M broker equity) and 10.7% of $1,764,000 (18% x $9.8M). Remarks: book value ($3.1M members' equity per year-end balance sheet) is 3.16x below broker equity ($9.8M) — the gap is presumably appreciated real estate not carried on the balance sheet (no appraisal in the file; confirm with client whether any company debt explains part of the gap). All percentages cross-checked: 0.061 x $3.1M = $189,100 exactly (the offer amount matches the diluted percentage only); 0.18 x $1.5M = $270,000 (Imani's unfunded share) and Bram's $1,230,000 + $270,000 = $1,500,000 (Bram subscribed 100% of the raise, consistent with him ending at 100% - 6.1% = 93.9%). REMAINING VALUATION UNKNOWNS: no independent corroboration of the broker opinion (it is an informal opinion of value, not a full appraisal) — commission a certified real-estate appraisal; company debt unconfirmed; book-vs-broker gap presumably unrecorded appreciation.
